routes.label: Bound the median and attain every candidate

question: Let \(R\) be a set of nine distinct integers. Six of the elements of the set are \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(6,\) \(9,\) and \(14.\) What is the number of possible values of the median of \(R?\)
solution:
For nine distinct numbers, the median is the fifth number in increasing order, with exactly four numbers on either side. Let this median be \(m\).

Only one fixed number, \(2\), is at most \(2\). Even if all three added numbers are smaller, there can be at most four numbers at most \(2\), so \(m\geq 3\). Also, the five fixed numbers \(2,3,4,6,9\) are at most \(9\), so the fifth number cannot exceed \(9\). Since the median is an integer, its only candidates are \(3,4,5,6,7,8,9\).

We must check that every candidate really occurs. For each proposed median below, add the indicated three integers to the six given integers:
\[
\begin{aligned}
m=3 &: \{-1,0,1\},\\
m=4 &: \{0,1,15\},\\
m=5 &: \{1,5,15\},\\
m=6 &: \{1,15,16\},\\
m=7 &: \{7,15,16\},\\
m=8 &: \{8,15,16\},\\
m=9 &: \{15,16,17\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Each row produces nine distinct integers with exactly four below the proposed median and four above it. Thus all seven candidates occur, and no other value can occur. The answer is \(\boxed{7}\), choice D.
